absent: Locking discipline for present, online, topology, IPI descriptor and AMU sample updates.
Definitions and numeric values of IPI kinds, NR_IPI, MAX_IPI, ipi_irq_base and nr_ipi.
Implementations of cross-call send, IPI descriptor lookup, scheduler, tick, work, backtrace, KGDB, crash-save, SDEI, DAIF, topology, NUMA, ACPI-presence and cpu-operations helpers.
Remainder of AMU tick handling and frequency-invariance setup, notifier, hotplug and sampling-period behavior beyond the truncated fragment.
Full kunwind walk algorithm, common unwind state layout, graph and kretprobe correction, and dump_backtrace entry point.
Sleep stack data layout, suspend enter and exit low-level transitions, and breakpoint restore assignment.
Syscall numbers, generated syscall header contents, and compat statfs structure layout.
Static-call instruction encoding details and literal-write failure consequences beyond warning.

findings.text: Early SMP setup initializes topology, records current CPU topology and NUMA membership, then returns immediately when requested maximum is zero without marking secondaries present. Otherwise for every possible CPU except self it looks up per-CPU operations, skips absent operations or failed preparation, marks present when firmware tables are disabled or report present, and records NUMA info.

Inter-processor interrupt space is indexed by eight logical kinds in fixed order: reschedule, call-function, stop, stop-NMI, timer broadcast, IRQ work, backtrace, KGDB roundup. Each index has an associated human readable trace label used by entry and exit tracing and by interrupt statistics display.

Interrupt statistics reporting iterates over all IPI indices and all online CPUs, printing per-CPU descriptor counters per index followed by the index label, then prints a single error line backed by a global error counter.

Generic call-function requests on a mask and on one CPU are both implemented by requesting a cross-CPU call with the call-function IPI kind. Reschedule for one CPU uses the reschedule kind. Timer broadcast on a mask uses the timer kind. IRQ work raise targets only the requesting CPU with the IRQ-work kind.

CPU stop through NMI never returns. It masks asynchronous exceptions including pseudo-NMI, optionally saves crash state when crash support and stop-on-crash are active and registers are available, acknowledges the request by marking the CPU offline, masks local SDEI, optionally attempts a dying transition when crashing, then enters a park loop.
Panic self-stop is a non-returning wrapper that invokes the NMI stop path with no register context and without forcing a dying transition on crash.

Backtrace request first tries a firmware SDEI cross-CPU NMI provider and returns if that provider handled the mask. Otherwise it falls back to a generic mask backtrace helper parameterized with a sender that issues the backtrace IPI kind. The fallback may therefore execute in non-NMI context.
KGDB roundup sends the KGDB IPI kind individually to every online CPU except the requester.

IPI dispatch validates the number against the supported count for tracing, then routes reschedule to scheduler handling, call-function to generic call-function handling, both stop kinds to NMI stop with current registers and dying enabled, timer to broadcast receive when broadcast is configured, IRQ work to work execution when configured, backtrace to CPU backtrace, KGDB to debugger callback, and unknown numbers to a critical log. Entry and exit tracing bracket only in-range numbers. The IRQ handler derives the logical number from the hardware IRQ minus a base modulo the IPI count and reports handled.

Spin-table boot keeps one physical release address per possible CPU. Initialization reads a per-CPU device-tree address property and reports a missing or invalid value. Preparation requires a non-zero address, maps it as cached normal memory covering linear and non-linear cases, stores the holding-pen physical address in little-endian order regardless of kernel endianness, cleans the cache range, wakes secondaries with an event, then unmaps.

Spin-table boot writes the logical identifier of the target CPU into a shared pen-release variable with cache clean to point of coherency, then wakes secondaries with an event. The operations table is named spin-table and binds init, prepare and boot callbacks described above.

Kernel unwind source is a five-valued enumeration distinguishing unknown, frame-derived, caller-derived, task-derived and register-PC origins. Unwind flags are a union of a full unsigned word with two one-bit indicators for function-graph and kretprobe influence.

Kernel unwind state contains a common unwind state, owning task pointer, graph index, source enumeration, flags union, register pointer, and when kretprobes are configured a list node for current probe tracking.

Unwind consumption uses callbacks returning whether to continue. Plain entry consumption forwards the current program counter. Reliable consumption refuses exception-boundary states derived from registers and otherwise behaves like plain consumption; the reliable walk is non-inline and non-instrumented. BPF consumption forwards program counter with zero stack pointer and current frame pointer through a BPF-specific cookie; its walk is likewise non-inline and non-instrumented and always targets current.

Backtrace printing annotates each address with a source letter: none for frame, C for caller, T for task, P for register PC, U otherwise, plus F when function-graph affected and K when kretprobe affected, enclosed in parentheses only when any annotation is present. EFI stack selection returns EFI info only when unwinding current inside EFI, otherwise unknown. Show-stack dumps a backtrace for the given task and enforces ordering with a barrier.
Native user frame tail is packed with a user frame pointer followed by a link register. Compat frame tail is packed with a compat frame pointer, a 32-bit stack pointer and a 32-bit link register.

Static-call patching substitutes a return-zero target when given a null function, decodes the literal address referenced by the trampoline using page-aligned base plus decoded offsets, writes the 64-bit target into that literal, and warns once on write failure. Tail flag does not alter the fragment behavior.

CPU suspend warns when system capabilities are not finalized, reports pending asynchronous memory-tag faults, saves interrupt and exception mask state while unmasking the interrupt controller priority mask for pseudo-NMI resume, pauses graph tracing, and enters idle accounting. Suspend path invokes the caller finisher and treats a zero return as not-supported; resume path exits idle accounting and runs suspend-exit restoration. Tracing is resumed and mask state restored before return. Boot allocation reserves one saved-context address per hashed MPIDR entry and warns on allocation failure.
Hardware breakpoint restore is held as a file-local function pointer taking a CPU number and returning status. The fragments show declaration only, not assignment or invocation.

Memory mapping entry rejects file offsets that are not page aligned and otherwise delegates with the offset converted to page units. Personality entry rejects 32-bit Linux personality when 32-bit EL0 is unsupported, otherwise delegates. Unimplemented syscall entry delegates to the generic not-implemented handler.

System-call tables are arrays of register-context handlers sized by the respective syscall count, prefilled with the not-implemented handler then populated from generated headers. The 64-bit table aliases personality to the arm64 personality handler and its compat-aware macro selects the native handler; the compat table compat-aware macro selects the compat handler.

32-bit compat statfs and fstatfs rewrite a size of 88 to 84 before delegating, preserving historic old-ABI sizing expectations. Compat mmap with 4K-unit offset rejects values with non-zero page-excess low bits, then shifts to native page units before delegating.
Compat 64-bit argument reconstruction offers two word orders for high and low halves, selected by endianness, and combines them by shifting the high half by 32 bits and adding the low half.

Profiling program-counter selection walks the current stack and skips addresses inside lock functions, returning the first address outside them or zero when none is found. Time initialization initializes clocks and timers, enables broadcast hrtimers, panics when the architected timer rate is zero, calibrates the delay loop from rate divided by timer frequency, and initializes paravirtualized time.

Frequency-invariance state comprises a per-CPU maximum-frequency scale word defaulting to capacity-scale squared, a CPU mask for frequency-invariance enablement, and per-CPU samples holding previous constant and core counter values plus last update time. Log lines from this component carry an AMU prefix.

Counter validity requires the CPU number to be within range and present, activity-monitor support present, and both previous counter snapshots non-zero, with debug diagnostics on each failure. Maximum-ratio setup rejects zero maximum or reference rates and zero computed ratios with one-time warnings, otherwise stores reference divided by maximum scaled by capacity-scale squared. Tick scaling refreshes references, ignores non-advancing counters, computes core delta times stored scale shifted and divided by constant delta, then clamps to capacity scale.

Unknown IPI numbers produce a critical per-CPU log without other recovery. A suspend finisher that returns success through the failure path is coerced to a not-supported error. Spin-table init failure on missing address property and prepare failure on mapping failure propagate device and memory errors respectively. Static-call literal write failure only warns.
